messages.subject: Re: Saturated model: How to interpret and write-up for results and discussion?
parts:
"Fit" in the chi-square sense only tells you about whether constraints (and supporting assumptions) hold. It tells you nothing about parameters that are freely estimated, so you haven't lost anything. Yu are in a regression world, so use that model for reporting your results.

On Sat, Dec 23, 2017 at 10:43 PM, Jordan H <jord...@live.ca> wrote:
Hi, I've just tested a simple mediation model (IV --> Mediator --> DV) using lavaan. After some research, I learned that I had a saturated or just-identified model with zero degrees of freedom and "perfect" fit statistics (e.g., CFI of 1, RMSEA of 0, etc.). I found an indirect effect in the predicted direction, but I'm unclear about how to proceed or write up my results from here. Is it appropriate for me to still report this effect, but just acknowledge that a limitation of interpreting this finding is that I cannot assess model fit due to a saturated model?

Any advice or alternative suggestions are appreciated, considering I'm just a Master's student who is still very new to SEM.

Thank you,
Jordan
